sources.title: McKinsey The state of AI in 2026
sources.population: 1,719 survey respondents across roles, industries and organization sizes in 97 countries; GDP-weighted
sources.denominator: 40%: respondents in organizations above USD 1 billion revenue; 22%: respondents in smaller organizations. Subgroup counts not verified; total n=1,719 is NOT either subgroup denominator.
sources.claim: Reported agent scaling differs by revenue size (40% versus 22%).
sources.scope: Agentic AI; cross-industry, not a freight-payment or municipal sample
sources.limitations: Self-report, selection and weighting limitations; revenue size is not employee count. Does not identify Rogers category or safety.
sources.locator: Key takeaways; Exhibit 2 discussion; About the research

sources.title: McKinsey The state of AI in 2025
sources.population: 1,993 respondents in 105 countries across organizational roles, sectors and sizes; GDP-weighted
sources.denominator: Overall AI-use figure: survey respondents, total n=1,993; not all firms in an economy. Function-level agent exhibit: n=1,933, asked of function users then rebased to total sample.
sources.claim: 88% reported regular AI use in at least one business function; this is not agentic or application-specific penetration.
sources.scope: Overall organizational AI; agent questions are separate measures
sources.limitations: Self-report; not a census. Do not combine function-level, any-function, scaling and fully-scaled measures.
sources.locator: Headline adoption discussion; About the research; report Exhibit 2

sources.title: Stanford HAI 2026 AI Index, Economy chapter
sources.publication_date: 2026 (exact release day not verified from the inspected primary page)
sources.fieldwork: Underlying corporate adoption observation year 2025; see M25
sources.population: Underlying McKinsey respondents; not a second independent Stanford survey
